scope.scopeNotesMd: This report is scoped to the core `boolean` primitive datatype StructureDefinition. It treats the R4 and R6 `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/boolean` artifacts as the same artifact because the canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, status, and abstract flag are stable. Per the inherited/base-artifact rule, the R6 introduction of `PrimitiveType` as the parent of primitive datatypes, and inherited `Element`/`Extension` constraint metadata changes, are recorded as out of scope rather than as local `boolean` findings.
outOfScope: The global R4-to-R6 primitive datatype class hierarchy shift where primitive datatypes now derive from `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/PrimitiveType` instead of directly from `Element` is not reported as a local `boolean` finding.

Inherited `Element.id`, `Element.extension`, `Element` constraint text, `Extension` constraint metadata, and removal of inherited `xpath` constraint metadata are delegated to the base `Element`, `Extension`, `DataType`, and `PrimitiveType` analyses.
Profiles, implementation guides, search parameters, operations, examples outside the core packages, and downstream language-specific generated models were not analyzed.

narrativeReportMd:
# boolean R4->R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No material local breaking changes were found for the `boolean` primitive datatype. The R6 StructureDefinition preserves the same canonical identity, primitive value element, cardinalities, FHIRPath type, `structuredefinition-fhir-type` metadata, and `true|false` regex used in R4.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 and R6 core `StructureDefinition-boolean.json` files, package metadata, package index identity entries, and the R6 `PrimitiveType` definition only to classify the base-hierarchy change. Inherited base-artifact changes are excluded from local findings as instructed.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 boolean instance content remains structurally acceptable in R6 at the local datatype level: values are still represented as `true` or `false`, the primitive value remains optional `0..1`, and primitive extensions remain available through the inherited extension mechanism. The main migration awareness item is not a boolean wire-format change but the R6 primitive type hierarchy, which belongs to the `PrimitiveType`/base datatype analysis.

## Highest-impact findings
None for local `boolean` changes.

## Findings requiring human review
None. Human review is only useful to confirm spec prose/change-note intent for the inherited primitive hierarchy change.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The local `boolean` model was effectively preserved. The one visible structural identity difference, `baseDefinition` moving from `Element` to `PrimitiveType`, is a cross-cutting base model refactoring and should be assessed once for the base artifact rather than duplicated here.

## Follow-up analysis
Review `PrimitiveType`, `DataType`, `Element`, and `Extension` reports for any validator or code generator impact from the new primitive superclass and inherited constraint metadata changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `boolean` has no material local R4-to-R6 breaking change. The value representation remains `true|false` with the same local element set and cardinalities. The only meaningful migration watchpoint is the inherited R6 `PrimitiveType` hierarchy, which is out of scope for this local report.
summary.migrationThemesMd: No data transform is needed for local `boolean` values. Validators, serializers, and code generators should continue to treat the primitive value as a Boolean and preserve primitive extension handling. Any class hierarchy updates caused by R6 `PrimitiveType` should be handled through base datatype migration work, not a boolean-specific transform.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local computable changes because both assigned StructureDefinitions are present and simple, and their snapshot element ids, cardinalities, types, regex, modifier flags, and summary flags compare cleanly. Confidence is slightly limited for explanatory intent because no official diff or rendered narrative pages were used.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Canonical URL, id, name, status, kind, type, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. The R6 `baseDefinition` changed from `Element` to `PrimitiveType`, but this is a cross-cutting primitive hierarchy change and is excluded from local findings by scope.
The snapshot element ids are unchanged: `boolean`, `boolean.id`, `boolean.extension`, and `boolean.value`.
All local and inherited snapshot cardinalities are unchanged: root `0..*`, `id` `0..1`, `extension` `0..*`, and `value` `0..1`.

`boolean.value` remains `http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.Boolean` with `structuredefinition-fhir-type` = `boolean`. `boolean.id` remains FHIRPath `System.String`, and `boolean.extension` remains `Extension`.
`boolean` has no `Reference`-typed elements or target profiles in either version.
`boolean` has no terminology bindings, so no value set, code system, or expansion comparison is applicable.

No local constraint was added to or removed from `boolean.value`. The visible `ele-1` and `ext-1` constraint text/xpath metadata differences are sourced from inherited `Element`/`Extension` definitions and are out of scope for this report.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value is defined for `boolean` in either version.
The primitive value regex is unchanged: `true|false`.
All compared `boolean` snapshot elements remain `isModifier: false`.
All compared `boolean` snapshot elements remain `isSummary: false` where the flag is present.
The `boolean` snapshots do not introduce local slicing changes. Inherited extension slicing behavior should be assessed in the base `Element`/`Extension`/`PrimitiveType` reports.

The root definition remains `Value of "true" or "false"`, and `boolean.value` remains `The actual value`. R6 metadata refreshes, such as publisher/contact/jurisdiction and the description dropping `Base StructureDefinition for`, do not change local boolean semantics.
`boolean.value` remains represented as an XML attribute and uses the same FHIRPath Boolean primitive type and regex. No local JSON/XML wire-format change was identified.
At the local datatype level, an R6 `boolean` value using `true` or `false` is representable in R4. No R6-only local element, type, value, or code was introduced.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Descriptive and stewardship metadata were refreshed without changing boolean value semantics
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes descriptive/stewardship metadata, including publisher/contact/jurisdiction/workgroup metadata and a shorter description (`boolean Type: Value of "true" or "false"`). These fields do not alter instance validation, allowed values, element cardinalities, or serialization.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Metadata consumers may see different publisher and package metadata in R6. This should not be treated as a data migration requirement for boolean values.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `boolean` derives from `PrimitiveType` instead of directly from `Element`. Any runtime or code generation impact from the new primitive superclass belongs to the `PrimitiveType`/base datatype analysis, not this local boolean report.

The visible constraint wording and `xpath` metadata differences on `ele-1`/`ext-1` are inherited from base artifacts and should be evaluated in the corresponding base reports if validator metadata compatibility is in scope.
